podcast.body: The Doobie Brothers covered this song in 1972, drawing inspiration from The Byrds' 1969 version rather than the 1966 original by Art Reynolds. Tom Johnston, a member of the band, stated that they had no intention of recording a gospel song, viewing themselves simply as "musicians outplaying a gig." The song entered the Top 40, peaking at number 35 in 1973. Live performances often attracted "one-wayers" who would point fingers skyward and throw scriptures onto the stage. "Jesus is just alright. It was released in 1972 on the album To lose Street. It's snuck into the top 40 at number 35 in 1973."
